params.name: p.reverse_speed_tolerance
params.convention: motion-detection convention: the magnitude below which a velocity component is measurement noise rather than travel, taken from the noise floor of positioning-derived speed
params.source: stationarity thresholds used in vehicle-trajectory datasets (NGSIM, highD processing: 0.2–0.5 m/s)

params.name: p.yaw_rate_tolerance
params.convention: yaw-rate resolution convention: the magnitude below which a rate-of-turn reading is sensor noise or the jitter of keeping a straight course; it names the source's resolution only
params.source: automotive-grade IMU yaw-rate noise and bias specifications (about 1 deg/s)

params.name: p.corner_reach
params.convention: reach convention: the distance within which a junction region counts as the road user's own corner, set to the corner radius of an urban street junction plus a passenger-car length
params.source: AASHTO Green Book minimum corner radii for urban intersections (4.5–9 m) and the P design vehicle length (5.8 m)

params.name: p.yield_conflict_horizon
params.convention: conflict-prediction convention of surrogate safety measures: the look-ahead within which the closest approach of two bodies is predicted from the velocities observed at the instant
params.source: FHWA Surrogate Safety Assessment Model (SSAM) time-to-collision thresholds (1.5–3 s)

params.name: p.yield_min_clearance
params.convention: conflict-prediction convention: the centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which the two bodies would be in conflict, set to the sum of two passenger-car half-diagonals plus a margin, since centre distance overstates a body clearance by about the two half-extents
params.source: SSAM conflict thresholds with AASHTO P design-vehicle dimensions (5.8 m by 2.1 m)

params.name: p.opposite_direction_tolerance
params.convention: heading-opposition convention: two designated carrier directions count as opposed when the cosine of the angle between them is below the negative of this ratio, that is when they differ by more than 120 degrees
params.source: the cosine tolerance the ontology's rel.oncoming contract uses for opposed headings

params.name: p.turn_window
params.convention: manoeuvre-recognition convention: the window behind the observation over which a turn's course change is taken, set to the time a passenger car takes to complete a junction turn at turning speed
params.source: AASHTO turning-path templates for the P design vehicle (a 90-degree turn at 15 km/h takes about 6 s)

params.name: p.turn_min_course_change
params.convention: manoeuvre-recognition convention: the smallest course change read as a turn rather than a bend taken or a lane change, set below the course change of the most skewed junction leg
params.source: AASHTO intersection design guidance (legs within 60–120 degrees of each other)

params.name: p.turn_max_course_change
params.convention: manoeuvre-recognition convention: the largest course change still read as a turn, set below a half turn so that a reversal of direction is not read as a turn to the left
params.source: AASHTO intersection design guidance and turning-path templates

params.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
params.convention: motion-detection convention: the speed below which a reading counts as no travel rather than movement
params.source: stationarity thresholds used in vehicle-trajectory datasets (0.2–0.5 m/s)

params.name: p.direction_reversal_window
params.convention: manoeuvre-recognition convention: the window behind the observation over which the course change of a reversal is taken, set to the time a passenger car takes to turn about at low speed, a multi-point turn included
params.source: AASHTO turning-path templates for the P design vehicle and observed U-turn durations (10–20 s)

params.name: p.direction_reversal_opposition_tolerance
params.convention: heading-opposition convention: the largest departure from an exact half turn still read as travelling back the way the road user came; the band is two-sided, a course change well beyond a half turn no longer leaving the vehicle in the opposite direction
params.source: lane-level map heading tolerances and the skew of opposing roadway alignments

params.name: p.curvature_resolution
params.convention: map-resolution convention: the curvature below which a roadway alignment is recorded as a tangent; it names the source's resolution only and sets no bound on how sharp a bend must be
params.source: highway alignment practice, where radii above about 1000 m are treated as tangent

params.name: p.crest_approach_reach
params.convention: stopping-sight-distance model: the reach from a crest region within which the crest withholds the view of the roadway beyond it, set to the stopping sight distance at ordinary highway design speed
params.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping sight distance (about 170 m at 60 mph)

params.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
params.convention: stop-point convention of the ontology's approach reading: the bound within which a halt counts as made at the named place, and beyond which the road user is outside the mark's stopping zone upstream; set to about half a passenger-car length so that a halt with the body at the mark counts and a halt a vehicle-length short of it does not.
params.source: stop-line and stop-bar placement practice in highway marking manuals (MUTCD-style stop-line setback), with the body-to-mark distance measured from the footprint.

params.name: p.intersection_view_sight_distance
params.convention: intersection-sight-distance model: the length of view along the intersecting way a halted driver needs before entering, taken as the departure sight distance for a passenger car entering a two-lane highway at ordinary arterial speed.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book intersection sight distance tables (Case B departure sight distance).

params.name: p.following_headway_min
params.convention: headway convention: the time headway a following driver needs to perceive the leader's deceleration and brake, so that the gap required is this time times the speed travelled; set to the two-second rule of driver-training and car-following practice for dry conditions.
params.source: car-following and perception-reaction practice (AASHTO 2.5 s brake-reaction time; the two-second headway rule of driver education).

params.name: p.following_headway_adverse_surface
params.convention: headway convention for adverse conditions: the time headway required where the surface, the weather or the road's alignment lengthens the stopping distance or shortens the view, taken as double the dry-condition headway, the customary wet-weather allowance.
params.source: wet-pavement stopping-distance allowances in highway design practice and the doubled-headway rule for rain, snow and ice.

params.name: p.following_traffic_density_count
params.convention: traffic-density convention: the number of traffic members present on the same highway at the observation at or above which the stream counts as dense, so that the adverse headway applies; set to the platoon size at which interaction between successive road users is continuous.
params.source: platoon and car-following density thresholds in traffic-flow practice.

params.name: p.same_direction_tolerance
params.convention: heading-alignment convention: two headings count as aligned when the cosine of the angle between them is above this ratio, that is when they differ by less than thirty degrees, the departure a lane change or a bend produces without ending travel in the same direction.
params.source: heading-tolerance practice for same-direction relations in trajectory analysis.

params.name: p.free_flow_min_speed
params.convention: traffic-stream convention: the speed at or above which the stream a road user travels in runs freely, so that a follower can open and hold a long space; below it the stream is queued and the space cannot be kept. Set to about a third of an ordinary rural highway speed, the breakdown speed of a congested stream.
params.source: speed-flow breakdown values in highway capacity practice.

params.name: p.pass_window
params.convention: manoeuvre-recognition convention: the window behind the observation within which the subject must have been behind the road user it is now going by for the movement to be read as one pass; set to the time a heavy vehicle takes to draw level with a vehicle it overtakes at a modest speed difference.
params.source: overtaking-manoeuvre durations in passing sight-distance practice.

params.name: p.gap_acceptance_headway
params.convention: gap-acceptance convention: the time headway a merging driver accepts in front of and behind itself, so that the space a third vehicle needs is its length plus twice this time at the speed of the stream; set to the headway a driver accepts when entering a moving stream.
params.source: critical-gap values for merging and lane-changing in highway capacity and gap-acceptance studies.

params.name: p.entering_vehicle_length
params.convention: gap-acceptance convention: the length allowed for the vehicle that is to enter and occupy the space, set to the design length of a passenger car, the shortest road user the words admit as entering.
params.source: passenger-car design-vehicle dimensions in highway geometric design practice.

params.name: p.procession_window
params.convention: configuration-recognition convention: the window behind the observation over which close succession must have held for a line of road users to be read as travelling together rather than as one vehicle momentarily catching another; set to a few car-following cycles.
params.source: platoon-identification windows in traffic-flow measurement practice.

params.name: p.procession_gap_max
params.convention: configuration-recognition convention: the largest longitudinal body gap at which successive road users are still read as travelling in one succession; set to the gap beyond which a following vehicle is no longer coupled to the stream ahead of it at ordinary rural speeds. It recognizes the configuration and sets no bound on how much space the duty requires.
params.source: platoon headway criteria in traffic-flow practice.

params.name: p.cautious_entry_speed_max
params.convention: intersection-entry speed convention: the crawl speed at or below which a driver entering a junction with no working control can halt within the short length of road it can see across the junction; set to about ten miles per hour, the speed highway practice treats as a cautious entry.
params.source: uncontrolled-intersection and limited-sight-distance entry speed practice in highway design and driver-training material.

params.name: p.simultaneous_entry_window
params.convention: simultaneity convention of junction conflict analysis: the largest interval between two entries into one junction at which the two are still read as made at approximately the same time, set to the time a passenger car takes to clear a small junction from its entry at ordinary entry speed, since entries farther apart than that leave no conflict for the right-of-way rule to resolve
params.source: junction capacity and conflict-analysis practice, where the critical headway for a crossing conflict at a minor junction is of the order of a couple of seconds

params.name: p.immediate_hazard_arrival_time
params.convention: gap-acceptance convention: the time within which an approaching vehicle's arrival at the junction leaves a driver crossing or turning across its path no acceptable gap, set to the time a passenger car needs to complete a turn or a crossing through an ordinary junction from a standing start
params.source: critical-gap values of junction gap-acceptance practice, where the critical gap for a left turn across opposing traffic is of the order of five seconds

params.name: p.yield_approach_speed_max
params.convention: yield-sign approach convention: the speed at or below which a vehicle approaching a yield sign counts as having slowed for the traffic it must yield to, set to the crawl speed from which a passenger car can halt within the stop-point tolerance of the place the sign governs
params.source: yield-control approach-speed practice, where a yielding vehicle is expected to approach at a speed from which it can stop within a car length, of the order of ten miles per hour

params.name: p.centreline_proximity_reach
params.convention: lane-width convention: the lateral reach from a road user within which the centreline counts as the mark its own half's innermost portion abuts, set to one urban traffic lane width, since a vehicle farther than a lane's width from the centreline has another line of vehicles' width of road between it and the centre
params.source: urban geometric design practice, where a through traffic lane is of the order of twelve feet wide

params.name: p.speed_reaction_time
params.convention: stopping-distance model: the perception and reaction time allowed before braking begins, during which the vehicle travels at its current speed
params.source: geometric design practice for stopping sight distance, which allows about two and a half seconds for an unexpected hazard and shorter times for an attentive driver anticipating one

params.name: p.speed_stopping_deceleration_dry
params.convention: stopping-distance model: the deceleration a passenger car achieves in a controlled emergency stop on a dry paved surface, which with the reaction time fixes the distance within which it can halt
params.source: geometric design practice for stopping sight distance, which uses a deceleration of about 3.4 m/s2 on a dry surface

params.name: p.speed_stopping_deceleration_adverse
params.convention: stopping-distance model: the deceleration a passenger car achieves in a controlled stop on a wet, icy or snow-covered surface or in falling precipitation, about half the dry value
params.source: wet and winter friction-factor practice, where available friction falls to roughly half of the dry value

params.name: p.reference_lane_width
params.convention: narrow-highway speed convention: the lane width at or above which the stopping and curvature bounds apply in full, below which they are reduced in the ratio of the width available to this reference
params.source: urban and rural geometric design practice, where a full through traffic lane is of the order of twelve feet wide

params.name: p.lateral_acceleration_max
params.convention: side-friction convention: the lateral acceleration a bend may impose on a passenger car at a reasonable speed, speed squared times curvature being that acceleration
params.source: horizontal-curve design practice, where the side friction factor assumed for comfort at highway speeds is of the order of 0.3 g

_fields.params: name (p.<name>), value (number), unit (m|s|m/s|m/s2|deg|deg/s|ratio|count), convention (text), figure_review (optional: why a value that equals a figure some law states is a convention, not that figure)
_fields.aggregates: word (a legal aggregate such as 'vehicle'), classes (ru.* ids it covers)
